thread:
maria (docs): Heads-up — I opened a docs PR for export retention language + CSV redaction examples. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482. Need security/legal signoff and a small Python/curl SDK snippet showing TTL header usage. Draft text is in the PR.
aj (security): SG. From security side, prefer limiting default retention to 90 days for exported audit slices. We can offer 30/90/365 presets. Also want a short paragraph explaining that exported files may be replicated outside our control.
kevin (legal): Agree with AJ. Important: don't promise deletion of copies once the customer downloads an export. Suggest wording: "Customers can configure export retention in the platform; Redwood retains exported copies for the configured period for as long as they remain in Redwood-managed storage. Copies downloaded and stored externally are the customer's responsibility."
maria (docs): Thanks — I'll replace the existing paragraph with that. Can someone provide the exact phrasing for the UI label and for the API header? Draft: `X-Redwood-Retention-TTL` for header and 'Export retention (days)' for UI. OK?
sasha (eng): We use `X-Redwood-Retention-TTL` in the pipeline, but note it's a best-effort signal for exported artifacts: the export job will set an S3 lifecycle tag, but if the export is downloaded, we can't enforce deletions. Also there's an edge-case where long-running exports may use different buckets.
kevin (legal): LGTM. Also recommend adding: 'Exported audit logs are delivered with metadata that indicates retention expiration and a checksum; customers should store and manage copies accordingly.'
maria (docs): Adding the sample snippets into the PR — please sanity-check.
```\ncurl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/exports/audit" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -H "X-Redwood-Retention-TTL: 90d" \\n  -d '{"range":"2026-02-01/2026-02-28","format":"csv"}'\n\n# Python\nimport requests\nheaders = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}", "X-Redwood-Retention-TTL":"90d"}\nresp = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/exports/audit", json={"range":"2026-02-01/2026-02-28","format":"csv"}, headers=headers)\n```
aj (security): One nit: use `90d` vs `90`? prefer ISO8601 durations `P90D` maybe. Our services accept both; docs should call out accepted formats: numeric days (e.g., `90`) or ISO `P90D`. Add that line.
sasha (eng): Implementation: backend accepts integer days and `P{n}D`. We normalize to int. I'll add a sentence to the PR.
docs-bot: Preview deployed: https://deploy-preview-482--docs.redwood.ai/export-retention
maria (docs): Perfect. Pinging @kevin and @aj for final signoff on the PR. If no objections by end of day I'll merge.
kevin (legal): :thumbsup: one tiny edit in PR comment re 'disposition' -> 'retention and disposition'. otherwise ok.
aj (security): :thumbsup: good from security.
